subject: Performance SLO + Private VPC: Post-call & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO + Private VPC: Post-call & next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our call on the Private/VPC performance qualification for Acme AI:

Summary of requirements you shared:
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 50ms for single-stream RPC calls (non-streaming inference).
- Streaming: support 95th percentile frame-to-frame latency <= 100ms for audio-gen pipeline (server->client streaming).
- Throughput & concurrency: baseline 400 concurrent inference sessions, burst to 1.2k for 30s bursts; target sustained throughput ~120 req/s with avg payload size ~3KB.
- Networking: VPN peering between Acme VPC and Redwood private subnet; expect egress NAT from Acme to Redwood; path includes a transit gateway and firewall inspection.

Open items / action owners:
1) Acme to share network topology and VPN config (Ravi) — we need IP ranges, expected MTU, and whether traffic will go through inspection appliances. (action: Acme, due: 2026-08-14)
2) Redwood to validate latency budget under expected path — we'll provide a short checklist of tests (traceroute, iperf3 for bandwidth, and 10k small-payload simulated requests). (action: Marissa/Jordan, due: 2026-08-17)
3) Schedule 30-min follow-up with network engineers to run a checklist and agree on MTU/keepalive settings. (action: schedule by 2026-08-15)

Attachments: acme-network-topology.pdf (please see attached topology), redwood-performance-slo-checklist.pdf (our suggested validation steps).

Proposed follow-up windows: 2026-08-16 09:00-10:00 PDT or 2026-08-17 11:00-12:00 PDT — let me know what works and I will set the invite.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.ai>, Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-14T11:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Private VPC: Post-call & next steps

Sam / Ravi —

Appreciate the quick turn. A few technical clarifications from our infra side before the network call:

1) Latency measurement points: we will measure p95 at two points:
   - client->redwood edge (RC endpoint IP) for single-request RTT (this captures transit + edge processing)
   - server-side inference loop (time spent in GPU inference loop) — Jordan will provide a synthetic test harness so we can separate network vs. server processing.

2) MTU and fragmentation: if Palo Alto is doing TLS inspection, we often see MSS reduction; please confirm if DF is set or if PMTU discovery is being altered. If MTU < 1400 we need to adjust our UDP/TCP segmentation settings for streaming frames.

3) Streaming behavior: for streaming (audio->text->audio-gen), we expect many small frames; please confirm expected frame size distribution (mean/95th). That will help Jordan tune batching and keepalive.

Action items (updated):
- Acme (Ravi) to confirm MTU, inspection bypass option, and expected frame size distribution by 2026-08-16.
- Redwood (Jordan/Aditya) to provision a test endpoint and send iperf/traceroute targets + synthetic harness by 2026-08-15.
- Both sides to join a 30-min network validation call — proposing 2026-08-17 11:00 PDT.

We can also run a quick proof-of-performance: 10k small-payload requests across the VPN at targeted concurrency and capture p50/p95/p99. That will help validate the p95 <= 50ms target and identify whether bulk of latency is network or server-side.

Thanks — I’ll send the calendar invite once Sam/Ravi confirm 8/17 works.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Sam Torres <sam.torres@acme.ai>, Ravi Patel <ravi.patel@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO + Private VPC: Post-call & next steps

Thanks for the notes — quick technical clarifications from my side.

On Fri, Aug 14, 2026 at 11:25 AM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> We can also run a quick proof-of-performance: 10k small-payload requests across the VPN at targeted concurrency and capture p50/p95/p99.

A couple things to call out so expectations are aligned:
- For non-streaming single-RPC calls, our validator will record end-to-end times from the client stub to when the last token is emitted by the model runtime. If there is server-side batching, that will add addnl ms; we'll run both batch-on and batch-off tests.
- For streaming, frame-to-frame latency is heavily impacted by MTU and TCP Nagle. If inspection appliances add head-of-line delays, the p95 can spike even if median looks fine.
- Recommended initial test matrix:
  * Traceroute + 3x iperf3 runs (1m)
  * 1k concurrent simulated sessions for 60s (small payloads)
  * 10k sequential small requests to collect p50/p95/p99

I can bring the synthetic harness and a small script to visualize latency tails during the call. If Acme can temporarily bypass inspection for the test we'll get a cleaner signal.

See you on 2026-08-17 if scheduled — otherwise we can move to next week.

Jordan
Infra Lead | Redwood Inference
